doc.title: Bob Stewart interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006

title: Charles Mingus: Taj Mahal tubas, big band albums, straw boss
summary: After Taj Mahal's four-tuba band, he joined Mingus's big band, played on two albums, and became Mingus's straw boss after breaking up a fight.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: I see. You spent some time with — well you’ve got a long, very interesting list of associates. Talk about Charles Mingus a little bit.

Sure. Sure. I got that gig in ’71, 1971. He put together, I think it was some anniversary of the big bands so he put the band back together in 1971. “71? ’72? ‘71 he put the band back together. Because I had just come off the road, that was the January I quit teaching, January of ’72 I quit teaching because I went out on the road with Taj Mahal. That’s when that happened. And we were doing Taj Mahal, the blues singer, he had this rock & roll blues band with four tubas in it and all of us doubled, that’s when the first time I played flugelhorn again, trumpet again, since I left it in college, I started playing again. I had forgot all the bad things and I could play it actually. It was great.

That time passed, I forgot how to do it wrong, and so when I picked it up I was doing it right, it worked. And Howard was doubling on flugelhorn and baritone saxophone and Joe Daly was tuba and valve trombone and Earl McIntyre was tuba and bass trombone. So we did that for the first four months of 1971, it was ’71. And then when that finished in April I was kind of like depressed because I mean it’s hard coming off one of those gigs where you’re playing for 5,000 people and 10,000 people, screaming and hollering, you know what I mean, you’re traveling posh, you know what I mean? You’re being escorted here and escorted there. Then all of a sudden there’s nothing. You know what I mean? So I’m sitting around patting my foot and looking at my watch and Howard Johnson calls me up and he says, “Mingus is putting a band together, he wants to use tuba and baritone man, come on down to such and so and so.” I said, “Yeah, cool.” And so they put the big band together and we did two albums. One was a live album at Avery Fisher featuring it was like Bill Cosby was the host and people like Gerry Mulligan and Gene Ammons was on the gig and he was just back to be able to play because he got his green card again. And there was a bunch of artists on there, I can’t even think of all of them right now, but it was an amazing gig. And then he did another studio album for Columbia called “Let My Children Hear Music” and there was a written solo with me and French horn, a duet on “Don’t Be Afraid, the Clown’s Afraid Too” which is great. So I got friendly with Mingus and one incident happened in the band where I had to break up a fight and Mingus was just floored by that, he said, “Did you see that man, did you see what he did?” I just picked up a cat and took him out of the room into the next room, and Mingus just loved that. He didn’t even try to stop the fight, he wanted to see how it was going to go and then I separated the cat and took him in the room, so Mingus hired me to
hire the band for that Avery Fisher Hall concert. And he was great to me, he was just as nice as he could be.
Yeah because people talk about how volatile he could be.

He was. He was just nice to me because he saw me do that so he figured I wasn’t one of the people he should be messing with. So he said well if he can do that, sure, he can control my band, so he hired me to do his straw boss, to hire cats for the next gig.
I’ll be darned. It could be the first time in history a straw boss played the tuba.

Right. I’m sure. I’m sure. But he was cool. I mean I heard little stories and everything about Bobby Jones and all the different cats that suffered under his hand, I watched him fire cats and before they could walk out the back door he hired them again. “Where you going? Bring your ass back here.” But he was great.
